title: Territorial data binding & KMS audit scope - NexaHealth
summary: Customer asked detailed questions about region pinning, customer-managed KMS/HSM options, audit scope for SOC2 and ISO, subprocessors and cross-border flows. Redwood AE + SE explained hosted vs private tradeoffs, KMS escrow/CMK options and what logs/audit artifacts are available. Agreed next steps: send subprocessor list, SOC2 + ISO reports, KMS onboarding guide, and schedule a short KMS test/bench next week.
topics: cross-border processing and Schrems II implications
transcript:
[00:00:02] Maya Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time, quick roll call?
[00:00:07] Daniel Ruiz: Daniel here, Head of Security at NexaHealth.
[00:00:09] Priya Shah: Priya, platform engineering.
[00:00:11] Olivia Martin: Olivia from legal.
[00:00:13] Tom Becker: Tom, infra.
[00:00:15] Maya Patel: Great. Ravi and Lena from Redwood are on too?
[00:00:18] Ravi Kapoor: Yep, Ravi here, will do the technical deep dive on KMS and audit logs.
[00:00:22] Lena Cho: Lena from CSM, I'll help with follow ups.
[00:00:26] Maya Patel: High level agenda — quick compliance checklist, KMS options, subprocessor mapping, then action items. Any additions?
[00:00:33] Olivia Martin: We mostly want to understand what proof artifacts we can get for audits, and whether data can be prevented from leaving EU boundaries.
[00:00:39] Daniel Ruiz: And we need to know where keys live — can Redwood use our KMS, or do we have to hand keys over, do you support HSM escrow?
[00:00:47] Ravi Kapoor: Yes, good questions. Quick note: I'll use some shorthand — when I say "Redwood Hosted" I mean the multitenant API, "Dedicated" is reserved GPU pools, and "Private" is customer VPC/on-prem. Some acronyms might get mangled in transcript, sorry in advance.
[00:01:04] Priya Shah: That's fine. Start with data residency, please.
[00:01:08] Ravi Kapoor: Sure. For territorial binding in Hosted, we provide region affinity — you can set EU-only routing and we maintain that for inference processing. However, control plane metadata (things like usage metrics and billing) may be in our control plane region. For strict EU-only processing we recommend either Redwood Dedicated in an EU region or Redwood Private (VPC) where control plane is routed per the DPA.
[00:01:33] Daniel Ruiz: Can you be explicit about cross-border backups, and any async processing that might touch data outside the EU? We need to avoid that for a particular product line.
[00:01:42] Ravi Kapoor: Right — by default we don't move PII out of the pinned region for inference payloads. Backups — snapshots of underlying storage for hosted are replicated based on our infra patterns which historically can cross regions; for EU-only requirements we advise Private with customer-managed storage or Dedicated with contractual guarantees. I'll put that in the notes: Hosted backups may be cross-region.
[00:02:01] Olivia Martin: What about subprocessors — do you publish an up-to-date list and can you commit to notifying us before additions?
[00:02:07] Maya Patel: We maintain a subprocessor roster. Standard is 30 days notice for new subprocessors and you can opt out per DPA with reasonable alternatives. We will share the current list as part of the follow-up pack.
[00:02:18] Priya Shah: KMS detail — can we bring our own CMK from our GCP KMS or AWS KMS?
[00:02:24] Ravi Kapoor: Yes. We support customer-managed keys via standard KMS integrations. Two modes: 1) Envelope encryption where you store the CMK in your KMS and Redwood fetches short-lived data keys; 2) Fully customer-hosted key service in Private deployments where Redwood never sees the key material. For Hosted multitenant, we support envelope CMK with a keywrap call; for Dedicated we can set up an option where the CMK is in your project and we exchange ephemeral key material.
[00:02:50] Tom Becker: Do you offer an HSM escrow in case of disaster recovery? We can't lose access if keys are only in our account and a human mistake happens.
[00:02:58] Ravi Kapoor: We have optional key-escrow patterns — typically customers provision an HSM-backed key with a split-control escrow handled via a support process. For high-security customers we can route keys through a BAA-approved HSM partner. There's an extra compliance review and SOW for that.
[00:03:13] Daniel Ruiz: Okay. For our auditors we need attestable logs showing key usage: who requested key unwraps, IPs, timestamps, and the exact object ID. Does Redwood surface that?
[00:03:23] Ravi Kapoor: Yes, we can surface key access logs. For envelope mode we can log KMS API calls and key wrapping/unwrapping events in audit logs — these come from your KMS if CMK is in your account, plus Redwood-side request logs that tie the inference request ID to the key event. For Private, you can retain full key logs in your environment.
[00:03:42] Olivia Martin: Are those logs immutable and exportable for ISO audits?
[00:03:47] Lena Cho: We provide log retention policies and can export compressed immutable bundles for audit windows. For ISO/SOC2 evidence we typically provide log bundles plus sign-offs. Some of that is in the SOC2 report itself.
[00:03:58] Daniel Ruiz: Speaking of SOC2, can you share your latest SOC2 and ISO certs and the scope? EU data handling needs to be clearly in-scope.
[00:04:05] Maya Patel: Absolutely, we'll include our SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 certs. Note the scope: hosted inference, control plane, and observability services are typically in scope; if you go Private with customer-managed infra, the scope shifts. We'll include the report and a short summary of scoping so your auditors can see what was tested.
[00:04:22] Priya Shah: If we use Hosted but pin region to Frankfurt, is there any transitive processing in US for model updates or telemetry?
[00:04:29] Ravi Kapoor: Telemetry and aggregated metrics may be aggregated in a central analytics cluster; RAW inference payloads remain in the pinned region. For strict regulatory needs we recommend Private.
[00:04:40] Tom Becker: What about endpoints for webhooks, logs, and callbacks — can you constrain egress to EU endpoints?
[00:04:46] Ravi Kapoor: Yes, webhook endpoints can be configured to an EU endpoint and if you use a VPC peering in Private, traffic stays in your VPC. For Hosted, callbacks are routed from the region but control plane metadata may route to central observability. We'll document specifics.
[00:04:58] Olivia Martin: On the DPA and SCCs — do you execute EU Standard Contractual Clauses and do you support Data Processing Addendum with EU-specific clauses?
[00:05:06] Maya Patel: Yes, we execute a DPA and implement SCCs where needed. We'll include current DPA language and the SCC annex.
[00:05:12] Daniel Ruiz: Is Redwood willing to sign additional flow-downs around subprocessors or a list of hard no's?
[00:05:18] Maya Patel: We can discuss that. For enterprise deals we do negotiable flow-downs and commitments on notifications.
[00:05:23] Priya Shah: Back to keys — latency: if we call KMS for every inference to unwrap, is that a perf hit?
[00:05:29] Ravi Kapoor: Good point. Envelope encryption uses a short-lived data key cached at the runtime level; we don't call KMS on every token. We call KMS on key unwrap for initial session setup and when rotating. So latency impact is minimal.
[00:05:44] Daniel Ruiz: What about key rotation and how that affects cache/KV state for models — can KV cache be re-encrypted without losing state?
[00:05:51] Ravi Kapoor: We support rotation strategies: rewrap on rotation or dual-key windows. Depending on the model and seq length we can preserve KV cache; it's a config option. We'll include recommended rotation patterns in the follow-up doc.
[00:06:05] Olivia Martin: For legal review we need to know retention periods and deletion certs. How do you prove deletion of customer data and cached prefixes?
[00:06:13] Ravi Kapoor: Deletion is logged and we can provide deletion certificates showing object IDs, timestamps, and deletion job IDs. For caching, we can evict KV entries and provide a log of evictions. For stricter needs, Private keeps cache entirely in your environment.
[00:06:27] Tom Becker: Can we get a test where we ingest a tagged payload and then request deletion and see the audit artifact?
[00:06:33] Maya Patel: Yes, we'll scope a KMS+deletion test as a short pilot with a small sample.
[00:06:37] Daniel Ruiz: Subprocessor question again: do you use third-party model-hosting vendors, e.g., for model weights and model updates?
[00:06:43] Ravi Kapoor: We orchestrate model downloads from curated registries. For hosted we may cache models in our storage tier; for private you control model artifacts. If a third-party is involved as a subprocessor, it's on the subprocessor list.
[00:06:56] Priya Shah: Regarding Schrems II, if our customers are EU citizens and keys are in US KMS, are there implications?
[00:07:03] Olivia Martin: (interjects) Schrems II is about transfer risk and access — key location matters a lot for our risk team.
[00:07:08] Ravi Kapoor: Correct. If keys are in the US, you have to evaluate the transfer risk. Our recommended pattern for low risk: CMK in EU region or Private deployment with EU key escrow. We'll include a short note on this in the follow-up pack mentioning SCCs and Transfer Impact Assessments.
[00:07:24] Daniel Ruiz: On monitoring for anomalous data exfil — can you gate model endpoints by RBAC and SSO groups?
[00:07:31] Ravi Kapoor: Yes, we integrate SAML/Okta for SSO and enforce RBAC on routes and API keys. You can also restrict which models or endpoints a team can call. We'll document the RBAC policy examples.
[00:07:43] Tom Becker: Are API keys stored plaintext in your system? That's a red flag for us.
[00:07:47] Ravi Kapoor: No — API keys are hashed at rest, and we only show the key once at creation. We also support short-lived tokens via OAuth flows for service-to-service.
[00:07:55] Priya Shah: For an SOC2 audit, the auditor will want to see evidence of least privilege and key handling. Will Redwood provide sample control mappings?
[00:08:02] Lena Cho: Yes, we have control mapping artifacts (SOC2 controls to our system features) and we can supply sample evidence snapshots for auditors under an NDA.
[00:08:11] Olivia Martin: Can we get a redlined DPA? We have some bespoke clauses.
[00:08:15] Maya Patel: We'll send over the DPA + a redline-friendly doc; legal can work directly if needed.
[00:08:20] Daniel Ruiz: Great. For the pilot test, can we scope the following: 1) EU KMS CMK in our GCP project, 2) a sample inference flow with a tagged payload, 3) deletion and certificate retrieval, 4) export of key access logs?
[00:08:33] Maya Patel: Yes, that's doable. Ravi, can you run the technical plan?
[00:08:36] Ravi Kapoor: I'll draft the pilot runbook — includes steps, expected artifacts, and a short benchmark for latency with envelope encryption. Expect a doc in 48 hours.
[00:08:45] Tom Becker: Nice. Any blockers on our side? We need to provision a test KMS key and give Redwood limited decrypt permissions.
[00:08:52] Priya Shah: We'll create a service account and a key with a binding for the pilot.
[00:08:56] Olivia Martin: Legal will review the DPA but no blockers otherwise.
[00:09:00] Maya Patel: Cool. Quick note on pricing for Dedicated/Private — there are platform fees for Private and a higher commit for Dedicated; we'll include ballpark numbers.
[00:09:09] Daniel Ruiz: For procurement we may need a list of subprocessors and data flows to onboard to our vendor risk platform.
[00:09:15] Lena Cho: We'll export a data flow diagram and the subprocessor csv.
[00:09:20] Olivia Martin: One more question on encryption: do you do in-flight TLS to the GPU nodes?
[00:09:24] Ravi Kapoor: Yes, TLS everywhere in transit; intra-cluster encryption is enabled by default and we can provide cipher suite details.
[00:09:33] Priya Shah: And do you store embeddings or token logs by default? We need to ensure PII isn't indexed inadvertently.
[00:09:40] Ravi Kapoor: Default hosted telemetry anonymizes payloads but we do retain limited token-level traces for debugging for a short retention window unless you opt-out. For strict PII controls, Private disables retention.
[00:09:53] Daniel Ruiz: Ok that's enough from our side. Can you recap next steps?
[00:09:58] Maya Patel: Sure — recap: 1) Redwood to send SOC2/ISO certs, DPA + SCCs, current subprocessor list, and KMS onboarding doc. 2) Ravi to share pilot runbook for CMK test within 48 hours. 3) NexaHealth to provision test KMS key and create service account. 4) Schedule pilot next week — Lena will propose slots.
[00:10:19] Lena Cho: I'll send a Doodle with three options.
[00:10:22] Olivia Martin: We'll look for the DPA and then loop in procurement.
[00:10:26] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and attach the docs.
[00:10:30] Daniel Ruiz: Thanks.
[00:10:32] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional transcription errors on technical terms, speaker overlap at 00:07:03. Some product names abbreviated.
